chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Hakam, who said:

I wrote to the Pious Servant (peace be upon him), informing him that I am doubtful, and Ibrahim (peace be upon him) had said: 'My Lord, show me how You revive the dead,' and I would like you to show me something.
So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Indeed, Ibrahim was a believer and he loved that there be an increase in his faith, and you are doubtful, and the one who is doubtful has no good in him.'
And he wrote: 'Doubt is only that which precedes conviction; so when conviction comes, doubt is not permissible.'
And he wrote: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: And We did not find in most of them any (faithfulness to) the Covenant, and We found most of them to be transgressors.'
He said: 'It was revealed regarding the one who is doubtful.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the doubt of Prophet Ibrahim and the doubt of a believer seeking knowledge?
ai.summary: In this epistle, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the doubt of the sincere seeker, exemplified by Prophet Ibrahim’s request for reassurance, and the stagnant doubt of the narrator, which lacks spiritual merit. He clarifies that doubt is a natural precursor to conviction but becomes impermissible once certainty is established, linking this state to the Quranic description of those who break their covenant. This hadith is foundational in Shia usul al-fiqh for understanding the transition from ijtihad (striving for proof) to taqlid or certainty.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Al Husayn Bin Al Hakam who said,

‘I wrote to Al-Abd Al-Salihasws (7th Imamasws), informing himasws that I am doubtful, and Ibrahimas had said [2:260] And when Ibrahim said: Lord! Show me how You Revive the dead, and I would like youasws to show me something’.
So heasws wrote: ‘Ibrahimas was a Momin and heas loved that there be an increase in hisas Emān, and you are doubtful, and the doubt it such that there is no good in it’.
And he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> wrote: ‘But rather, the doubt is what the conviction does not come to. So when the conviction does come, the doubt is not allowed’.
And heasws wrote: ‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [7:102] And We did not find in most of them any (faithfulness to) the Covenant, and We found most of them to be as transgressors.
He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘It was Revealed regarding the doubt’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from al- Husayn ibn Hakam who has said the following:

“Once I wrote to the virtuous servant (of Allah) saying that I had doubt and Ibrahim, peace be upon him, had said, ‘Lord, show me how you will bring the dead to life?’ (2: 260) and I would love that you show me something.
The Imam wrote back to me, ‘Ibrahim was a believer. He wanted to increase his belief. You, however, have doubt and there is nothing good in doubt.’
The Imam further wrote, ‘Doubt comes when there is no certainty when certainty, comes then doubting is not permissible.’
He wrote further, ‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, “We did not find many among them keeping their promises. However, We did find many evil-doers among them.” [7:102]
The Imam said, ‘It was revealed about people who doubt.’”
